observations.statement: catalog.project_new_github_repo is mapped to cmd.project.new_github_repo and handlers::github::project_new_repo on the project-creation/GitHub surface, with github.repo.create_requested and project.github_repo_bound as its expected events.

The GitHub repository command requires pre-dispatch exposure of auth, permission, owner-selection, approval, and duplicate-repository disabled reasons; receipt evidence must preserve repository and project-binding identities, correlation, remote outcome, and a recovery route; named regressions cover five negative cases.
The GitHub repository command reads a named availability selector and disabled-reason projection, and its effect contract requires both declared events plus dispatch-correlation evidence.

catalog.project_new_local maps to cmd.project.new_local and handlers::project::new_local; it has no declared persisted event and instead names a dispatch-receipt effect and a test oracle forbidding unexpected persisted domain events.

catalog.project_open maps to cmd.project.open and handlers::project::open; it has no declared persisted event and instead names a dispatch-receipt effect and a test oracle forbidding unexpected persisted domain events.
catalog.remote_reconnect maps cmd.remote.reconnect to handlers::remote::reconnect and requires remote.reconnect.requested plus command metadata in event evidence.

catalog.runtime_abort_run is an Abort Run action mapped to handlers::runtime::abort_run; its canonical effect is goal_run.stopped, dispatch correlation is required, and placeholder command_applied events are invalid.

catalog.runtime_approve is an Approve action mapped to handlers::runtime::approve; its canonical effect is node.unblocked, dispatch correlation is required, and placeholder command_applied events are invalid.

Every command in the core has an accessibility contract covering stable role/name/description, keyboard reachability and activation, visible-focus handling, deterministic focus return after dispatch or error, and assistive announcement of the projected disabled reason.

Production certification is explicitly conditioned on render/control, dispatcher, typed payload/result, projected state, disabled-reason, effect, accessibility, and regression evidence, with GitHub-specific create/bind and receipt assertions.

candidate_findings.title: Typed command contracts are asserted without exact schemas
candidate_findings.statement: The core repeatedly requires typed arguments, payloads, and results, but it does not define any command's payload fields, result variants, field types, requiredness, validation rules, or error representation.
candidate_findings.impact: Independent UI, dispatcher, and handler implementations can adopt incompatible wire shapes while each claims conformance, leaving the dispatcher fixtures and production-certification oracle non-deterministic.

candidate_findings.title: GitHub create-and-bind ordering and partial failure are unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: cmd.project.new_github_repo requires two persisted event types, but the core does not state their required ordering, atomicity, causation relationship, or the outcome when remote repository creation succeeds and project binding fails; retry and idempotency semantics are also absent.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can produce orphaned repositories, duplicate remote side effects, or divergent project bindings while still emitting both named event types.

candidate_findings.title: GitHub gating and recovery behavior is enumerated but not resolved
candidate_findings.statement: The GitHub command names pre-dispatch conditions and negative cases, but it does not define their state transitions, disabled-reason precedence, exact dirty-project or user-declined outcomes, or the behavior of the required recovery route.
candidate_findings.impact: Equivalent failures may be enabled, disabled, messaged, retried, or recovered differently across implementations and tests.

candidate_findings.title: Eventful commands retain a contradictory no-persist alternative
candidate_findings.statement: cmd.remote.reconnect, cmd.runtime.abort_run, and cmd.runtime.approve each allow an explicit route/open no-persist disposition as an alternative to a typed payload/result contract even though their effect contracts require an event. The core does not resolve which branch is certification-authoritative.
candidate_findings.impact: A builder or test could treat a no-persist route disposition as sufficient while omitting the mandatory reconnect, stop, or unblock event.

candidate_findings.title: Local and open receipt oracles are disjunctive
candidate_findings.statement: For cmd.project.new_local and cmd.project.open, effect_kind is receipt and a dispatch_receipt ref is named, yet the description and event-test oracle accept either a receipt or a route/open disposition. The required artifact, schema, and observability guarantee are therefore not singular.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations can preserve materially different audit trails, making production evidence incomparable and command outcomes harder to reconcile.

candidate_findings.title: Reconnect lifecycle and failure contract stop at request emission
candidate_findings.statement: cmd.remote.reconnect defines dispatch and remote.reconnect.requested, but it does not define connecting, retrying, connected, or failed state transitions; retry/backoff limits; cancellation; duplicate suppression; or visible failure and recovery behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: The UI and runtime can disagree about connection truth, issue concurrent reconnects, retry indefinitely, or provide no deterministic recovery path.

candidate_findings.title: Abort Run lacks cancellation and terminal-timing semantics
candidate_findings.statement: cmd.runtime.abort_run maps to goal_run.stopped but does not define cancellation propagation to in-flight work, graceful versus forced termination, cleanup ordering, event-emission timing, repeated-abort idempotency, or partial-failure handling.
candidate_findings.impact: A run can be reported stopped while work or side effects continue, and repeated aborts can create divergent state or evidence.

candidate_findings.title: Approve lacks authority, target, and concurrency semantics
candidate_findings.statement: cmd.runtime.approve maps to node.unblocked but does not define approval authority, target-node identity, blocked-state preconditions, approval provenance, repeated-approval behavior, or serialization of concurrent unblock attempts.
candidate_findings.impact: An implementation could unblock the wrong node, accept unauthorized or stale approval, or emit duplicate and conflicting state transitions.

candidate_findings.title: Required regression evidence has no behavior-specific negative cases
candidate_findings.statement: Although production certification requires regression test evidence, the local, open, reconnect, abort, and approve test_evidence arrays name only dispatcher, state, effect, accessibility, and, where applicable, event assertions; they supply no behavior-specific negative or failure scenarios with expected outcomes.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders must invent failure coverage and acceptance behavior, so materially incomplete or incompatible implementations can generate superficially similar certification packets.

candidate_findings.title: Deterministic focus return has no specified destination
candidate_findings.statement: Each accessibility contract requires deterministic focus return after dispatch or error, but no return target or conditional focus rule is specified for either outcome.
candidate_findings.impact: Controls can all pass a general focus assertion while producing inconsistent keyboard and assistive-technology workflows.

candidate_findings.title: Availability projections lack a state model
candidate_findings.statement: The availability and disabled-reason paths are named, but their data types, allowed availability states, transition triggers, disabled-reason priority or composition, freshness, and owning authority are not defined.
candidate_findings.impact: UI enablement and disabled explanations can diverge across surfaces or become stale relative to handler preconditions.

candidate_findings.title: Correlation and receipt semantics are only field-level
candidate_findings.statement: The core requires dispatch evidence to preserve command identity, origin, correlation, handler target, result, and an effect, but it does not define correlation_id uniqueness or scope, receipt persistence or durability, duplicate reconciliation, or how receipts relate to emitted events.
candidate_findings.impact: Receipts and events may not support reliable deduplication, causal reconstruction, or recovery after partial failures.

candidate_findings.title: Event acceptance omits domain payload assertions
candidate_findings.statement: The event tests assert event type plus command_id, origin, correlation_id, and handler target, but state no domain payload requirements for repository creation and binding, reconnect requests, stopped runs, or unblocked nodes.
candidate_findings.impact: Tests can pass when an event names the correct type but identifies the wrong repository, project, run, or node, or lacks the data consumers need.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: The core gives an explicit UI element, user-facing location, command ID, and handler target for each of the six catalog entries.
Each command has a named availability selector and disabled-reason projection rather than leaving the pre-dispatch state source entirely implicit.
The GitHub repository command explicitly names both expected event types, the receipt identities and outcome fields, five regression cases, and event-test correlation metadata.
cmd.project.new_local and cmd.project.open explicitly declare no persisted event, name dispatch-receipt references, and require tests to reject unexpected persisted domain events.
Reconnect, Abort Run, and Approve have explicit expected event types and event-test requirements carrying command_id, origin, correlation_id, and handler target.
Abort Run and Approve explicitly reject placeholder command_applied effects and identify goal_run.stopped and node.unblocked as canonical domain events.
Role/name/description, keyboard activation, visible focus, post-dispatch or error focus return, and disabled-state assistive announcement are all explicit accessibility obligations for every entry.
The core names multiple production evidence classes rather than treating registration alone as certification.

unknowns.statement: It is unknown from this window whether exact command payload and result schemas are defined elsewhere.
It is unknown whether a route/open disposition is itself persisted, how it is shaped, or whether it is considered equivalent to the named dispatch receipt.
It is unknown whether the two GitHub events are ordered or transactional under a contract outside this window.
It is unknown whether reconnect completion and failure use later events, state projection changes, or only an out-of-band result.
It is unknown whether goal_run.stopped means an abort request was accepted or all run activity has actually terminated.
It is unknown which actor or policy may approve, how the target node is identified, and what approval provenance is retained.
The exact accessibility role, accessible name, description text, and focus-return destinations are unknown from the generic accessibility clauses.
It is unknown what values each state.commands.*.availability selector can take or how simultaneous disabled reasons are selected.
It is unknown whether correlation identifiers have uniqueness, idempotency, or causal-scope rules defined outside this window.
